**Triage: lands in `packages/types/src/zod/layout.zod.ts` + `packages/types/src/layout.ts` + `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`; `domain:spec`; `Bug`; `priority:p2`; `pm:blocked`.** `finding` removed — 定级即离标.

**`Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#16929`** (its PR #17835 is the retirement; the card measured it **unmerged**, contract review FAIL, patch round at `4d55c069c`). ⇒ genuine upstream wait. ⛔ Not dispatchable, and the card's own fence is adopted verbatim: **⛔ do not sequence work here assuming the spec side has landed.**

Routing: `packages/types` + the schema corpus is objectui's **contract face** ⇒ `domain:spec`. ⭐ Cross-repo placement was already correct — surfaced by objectstack's spec seat, filed here because the fix lands here.

### p2 rationale — ⛔ graded on what the declaration TEACHES, not on what breaks

The card is scrupulous that ⛔ nothing breaks today, and it is right. I am grading above that anyway:

⭐ **This is not lag — it is instruction.** objectui declares the key **authorable** (a page document carrying it parses clean here) *and* describes it as **`"Profiles that can access this page"`**, in a `describe()` that reaches generated reference docs, plus a shipped docs table. Meanwhile ADR-0090 D2 removed the Profile concept outright — 「`isProfile` deleted, **not deprecated**」 — and the producing side turns the key into a tombstone that **refuses any value**.

⇒ an author reading objectui's own reference is taught to reach for an **access-control mechanism** that (a) names a concept the platform deleted and (b) the producer refuses. ⚠️ The security flavour is what moves this off p3: 「这个页面谁能访问」 is exactly the kind of key an author sets **and then stops worrying about**. A key that reads as access control and enforces nothing is worse than an absent one, because absence prompts a question and a false declaration answers it.

⚠️ **Scope of that claim, stated so it is not overread**: ⛔ this card does **not** establish that any page is wrongly exposed today, and ⛔ I have not measured whether anything in this repo *reads* `assignedProfiles`. The defect as measured is **declared-and-described ≠ enforced-anywhere**, ⛔ not a live authorisation bypass. ⇒ ⛔ do not escalate it as a security incident, and ⛔ do not downgrade it to a docs typo either.

### ⚠️ Why the drift guard will not save you here

> objectui's drift guard asserts key **presence**, not type, so the spec-side tombstone does not turn it red.

⭐ That is the whole reason this can sit unnoticed, and it generalises: **a presence-only guard cannot see a key whose meaning was retired underneath it.** Whoever takes this should say, in the PR, whether that guard gap is worth its own card — ⛔ but do **not** widen the guard on this card.

### ⛔ Direction deliberately left open — and one option ruled OUT

The card offers: remove · tombstone in step · re-describe toward the permission-set route. ⛔ Triage does **not** pick — it depends on when `.objectstack-sha` advances past PR #17835, and the producer's final shape is not settled while that PR is in a patch round.

⭐ **One arm is ruled out now, so it is not rediscovered later:** ⛔ **leaving the `describe()` text as-is under any of the three routes.** Whatever happens to the key, the sentence 「Profiles that can access this page」 must not survive — it names a deleted concept and is the half that actually reaches authors. 说明书脱节 with a ruling in hand (ADR-0090 D2) is 改文档, and that part needs no further decision.

⚠️ **Unblock criterion — verify the PRODUCER, ⛔ not the merge button**: when objectstack#16929 closes, re-verify against the **installed/pinned** spec that `page.assignedProfiles` actually refuses a value before dispatching — 跨仓解锁判据是消费方可安装,⛔ 不是上游已合并. The same trap objectui#8945 fell into twice this week.

⚠️ Line numbers: the card gives `origin/main` (`:707`, `:1152`, `:141`) **and** the pinned checkout (`:405`, `:741`, `:126`), and says both are real and both will rot. ⇒ re-locate by symbol, ⛔ not by line.

### ⭐ On the re-filing

Second card this batch rebuilt after the `os-musk` suspension destroyed the original, and again **re-measured rather than restored from memory** — including a fresh lit control (`permissionSet` / `PageSchema` resolve) and a dark control (fresh token → 0). ⛔ Never restore a destroyed card from memory; this is how it is done instead. Fleet-wide record of the suspension's cost: objectstack#18052.

`Size/model suggestion:` M — three files, but it touches a published schema's acceptance set ⇒ the taker declares `Clause-②` on the real diff, not on this note.

## Half-state repaired, and the card's blocking premise is STALE — unlock scan, R2 patrol

`domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat, session `session_01VCpmqvacV4BypY48QdoxcE`, 2026-09-16T11:02Z.

### ⛔ The half-state: this card was invisible to the unlock scan

This card is **`pm:blocked` with a `Blocked-by:` line in NEITHER channel** — not in the body, not in any comment. The unlock sweep greps that literal line, so nothing could ever have returned this card to the queue: the block would have outlived its blocker in silence. That is the patrol's **H4** shape, measured here rather than inferred.

⚠️ **And the reason the comment channel is empty is itself worth recording.** This issue's `comments` field reads **1**, while both the MCP listing and `GET /issues/9409/comments?per_page=100` return **0** (lit control: `GET /issues/8961/comments` returns **8** on the same instrument, same call batch). The body explains it — 「the original was destroyed when the `os-musk` identity was suspended」. ⇒ **a suspended author's comment is still COUNTED but not SERVED.** So 「read the thread to the last page」 can silently miss content, and a count-vs-content mismatch is the only signal there was ever anything there. Filed to objectstack#18426 with the other platform readings.

### ⭐ The stated blocker has CLOSED — and the card would have misled the next reader

The body says, verbatim:

> ⚠️ objectstack PR #17835 is **not yet merged** — its contract review returned FAIL on unrelated grounds and a patch round has pushed `4d55c069c`. ⛔ Do not sequence work here assuming the spec side has landed.

Measured 2026-09-16T11:02Z: **objectstack PR #17835 is MERGED** (`merged_at` **2026-09-14T00:03:48Z**) and **objectstack#16929 is CLOSED**. ⇒ that paragraph is **stale**, and a reader taking it at face value would either park this card forever or, on discovering the merge, conclude it is ready. **Neither is right**, because of the next reading.

### ⛔ But merged is NOT the unlock criterion — and it is not installable

`SKILL.md` 〈多仓协调〉: 「跨仓解锁判据是消费方**可安装**,⛔ 不是上游已合并 … 未发版 ⇒ 转 `pm:on-hold` + `Restart-when:` 加消费方安装面判据,⛔ 不回 `pm:queue`。」

| reading | value | taken from |
|---|---|---|
| `@objectstack/spec` **17.4.0** published | **2026-09-09T03:57:51Z** | npm registry `time` |
| `@objectstack/spec` **17.3.0** published | 2026-09-04T10:52:49Z | same |
| npm `dist-tags.latest` | **17.4.0** | same |
| PR #17835 merged | **2026-09-14T00:03:48Z** | GitHub |

⇒ the retirement landed on `main` **five days after the most recent publish**, and nothing has been released since. **The retirement is unpublished.** ⛔ There is no version for objectui to move to — the same shape this lane measured today on objectui#8831, which is now on hold for the same reason.

ℹ️ One further reading, stated as a reading and ⛔ not as a conclusion: on objectstack `origin/main` the retirement's migration entries are named `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/**18**.ui__Page__assignedProfiles.ts` and `entries/semantic/**18**.page-assigned-profiles-audience-to-permission-set.ts`. The `18.` prefix **suggests** this retirement is slated for major **18**, i.e. gated on a major release rather than any patch publish. ⛔ This seat did not verify what that prefix binds, and whoever picks this card up should establish it before assuming a routine bump will deliver it.

### State transition — `pm:blocked` → `pm:on-hold`

`pm:blocked`'s unlock predicate is "the `Blocked-by:` target closed". Both candidate targets are **already closed**, so that predicate is spent while the card is genuinely not actionable — which is precisely the state the rule routes to `pm:on-hold`.

**Blocked-by:** objectstack-ai/objectstack#16929 *(recorded for the reverse index; ⚠️ already CLOSED, so it is history, ⛔ not a live gate)*

**Restart-when:** objectui's **installed** `@objectstack/spec` refuses `page.assignedProfiles`. One-line predicate, run from an objectui worktree with dependencies installed — **exit 0 ⇒ restart**:

```
node --input-type=module -e "import('@objectstack/spec/ui').then(m=>{const r=m.PageSchema.safeParse({type:'page',assignedProfiles:['x']});process.exit(r.success?1:0)})"
```

⛔ An **install-surface** predicate by design: ⛔ not "objectstack merged it" (already true, and insufficient) and ⛔ not "a new version exists" (necessary but not sufficient until objectui's lockfile resolves to it).

**Pre-written dispatch shape for when it fires**, so the next seat does not re-derive this:
1. Run the predicate; it must exit 0 first.
2. Establish what the `18.` prefix binds — patch publish or major 18.
3. The three declaring sites, re-derived by symbol (⛔ the card's line numbers have already been recorded as rotting): `packages/types/src/zod/layout.zod.ts` · `packages/types/src/layout.ts` · `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`.
4. ⚠️ The `describe()` reaches generated reference docs, so the docs table is part of the diff, ⛔ not collateral.
5. Direction follows the maintainer's standing 「以 objectstack 协议为准」 — but the card states no prescription and this seat adds none.

## Hold re-verified — still held, and the unlock is now a NAMED, measured action

`2026-09-17T14:46Z` · PM seat `domain:spec` @ objectui · `Seat: domain:spec#1` · session `session_01UanLVj6xvbS6puBCewLr8L`

Standing unlock scan. The gate has not opened, but it is no longer 「waiting on an unpublished spec」 in the abstract — it is waiting on one identifiable pull request, and the change this card needs is **provably inside it**.

**This card's change, tracked to the release:** `.changeset/16929-page-assigned-profiles-removed.md` and `.changeset/page-guidance-stops-prescribing-assignedprofiles.md` are both on objectstack `main` and both read `status: removed` in objectstack#17076 ⇒ consumed by that release run. The retirement itself is implemented on objectstack `main`: `page.assignedProfiles` resolves **8** hits under `packages/spec/src` — the migration entry `migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__Page__assignedProfiles.ts`, the conversion-registry surface at `conversions/registry.ts:9525` with its removal message, and the protocol docblock — beside a **lit control** of `PageSchema` at **32** files and an **absent-token control** at **0**.

## The shared evidence, measured this act

All on `origin/main` of both repositories, fetched by this act.

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| `@objectstack/spec` npm **`latest`** | **17.4.0**, published `2026-09-09T03:57:51Z` — unmoved for 8 days |
| `packages/spec/package.json` on objectstack `main` | **17.4.0** — not yet bumped |
| open release PR **objectstack#17076** (`chore: version packages`) | bumps `packages/spec/package.json` **`"version": "17.4.0"` → `"17.5.0"`** |
| its file list | **541 files**, enumerated to completion over 6 pages (page 6 returned 41 < 100, so the pagination terminated rather than being cut) |
| `.changeset/*.md` entries in that diff | **381**, of which **381** are `status: removed` — `changeset version` deletes a declaration it consumes, so `removed` is the positive reading |
| **absent-token control** on the same file list | **0** |

⚠️ The first read of that file list returned **exactly 100** entries — the page cap. ⛔ A "not found" out of a capped list is not a reading; it was re-taken with pagination before anything below was concluded.

⇒ **the unlock for this card is one human action: objectstack#17076 merging, and `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0 publishing.**

⛔ **Not taken, and not takeable by this seat:** running a release and merging a Version Packages PR are both on the PM red-line list. ⛔ No release was run, no release PR was touched, and the existence of a mechanical route is not authorisation.

## ⛔ The hold is NOT released

The predicate on the latest hold comment is a **consumer-installability** one — 「objectui's **installed** `@objectstack/spec` …」 — which is the correct cross-repo spelling: 跨仓解锁判据是消费方可安装,⛔ 不是上游已合并. The installed version is still 17.4.0, so the predicate is still **false** and the card stays `pm:on-hold` with its `Restart-when:` line unchanged.

⚠️ This seat did **not** probe the installed package: the shared checkout `/home/user/objectui` has no `node_modules`, and a resolution probe there returns a dead-instrument zero. ⛔ That zero was not read. The npm-registry reading above is what stands in for it, and it is sufficient in one direction only — `latest` is below 17.5.0, so nothing installable can carry the change yet.

⭐ Also checked and found correct rather than fixed: this card carries no `Restart-when:` line in its **body**, only in a comment. `references/state-machine.md` line 15 makes 「正文**或评论**」 legitimate, so this is ⛔ not a half-state. Recorded because this seat started to "repair" it before reading the rule.


## 维护者速读

**一句话** —— 这张卡等的上游改动**已经做完并合进 objectstack `main`**,也已经被写进待发布声明;它只差**一次发布**。发布 PR objectstack#17076 开着,会把 `@objectstack/spec` 从 17.4.0 升到 **17.5.0**,而这张卡需要的那两份声明**确实在这次发布里**(实测:两份都已被该 PR 消费)。npm 上的 `latest` 停在 17.4.0 已经 **8 天**。

**你要做的** —— 没有要您裁的事,只有一个信息:**合并 objectstack#17076 会同时解锁本卡与 objectui#8831 两张 p2**。⛔ 本席不合并发布 PR、不跑发布 —— 那在红线上。

**H9 repair — the `Restart-when:` line is replaced with a machine-fireable one.** `domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat · `session_01UanLVj6xvbS6puBCewLr8L` · 2026-09-18T14:30Z

⛔ No label written — the card stays `pm:on-hold`, which is the right state. ⛔ Nothing about the ruled option (a) is reopened. What changes is only the **exit**, which until now was prose naming no issue, no tracked path and no runnable command — 「a `manual` in disguise」, so nothing scheduled the actor this card waits on.

## The exit, machine-fireable — this supersedes the prose exit above

Restart-when: `node -e "import('@objectstack/spec/ui').then(m=>{const r=m.PageSchema.safeParse({name:'p',type:'object',assignedProfiles:['admin']});process.exit(!r.success&&JSON.stringify(r.error.issues).includes('assignedProfiles')?0:1)},()=>process.exit(1))"` exits 0 against this repo's INSTALLED `@objectstack/spec` — i.e. the installed spec REFUSES the key by name

⚠️ Run it in a worktree with a real install, and ⭐ **pair it with a lit control in the same run** — a page document WITHOUT the retired key must parse green in the same run, and a key nobody ever declared must be refused the same way. ⛔ Without both, an exit 1 cannot be told apart from a broken import, and an exit 0 cannot be told apart from a door that refuses everything.

## Why the predicate is installability and ⛔ not 「upstream merged」

Measured on `objectstack-ai/objectstack` `origin/main` = `abb01f105ceeb05ccab729dae9f46a009f3342eb`: the retirement is present and named: `packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts:9533` carries `surface: 'page.assignedProfiles'` with the message 「page key 'assignedProfiles' removed (ADR-0090 D2 deleted the Profile concept it was named after)」, and `:9508` dates it 「removed (protocol 18, ADR-0090 D2 / ADR-0049)」.

⇒ merged upstream, and ⛔ **not installable here**:

| reading | value |
| --- | --- |
| npm `dist-tags` for `@objectstack/spec` | `latest` = **17.4.0** |
| ⭐ LIT CONTROL — total published versions | **166**, ending `17.0.0` · `17.1.0` · `17.2.0` · `17.3.0` · `17.4.0` ⇒ the registry answered, so the next row is a reading |
| published `18.x` versions | **0** |
| this repo's pin, `origin/main` | root `^17.0.0` · `packages/types` `^17.4.0` |

⇒ there is **no version to move the pin to**.

## ⚠️ This is one blockage wearing four cards, ⛔ not four independent holds

objectui#8831 (`allDayField`) · objectui#9409 (this card, the `page.assignedProfiles` retirement) · objectui#9111 (`checkDashboardWidgetStageOrder`, moved to `pm:on-hold` in this same round) — and objectui#8979 already waits on a spec bump by name.

⭐ Measured, and it names the major: the `page.assignedProfiles` conversion entry on `objectstack` `main` reads verbatim 「removed (**protocol 18**, ADR-0090 D2 / ADR-0049)」, and `checkDashboardWidgetStageOrder`'s migration entries carry the `18.` file prefix. ⇒ all three ride the **unpublished major**.

⛔ That root cause is **not this seat's to fix** — ⛔ this seat does not run releases. It is raised to the maintainer; recorded here so the cards read as one blockage.

⚠️ ⛔ **Not measured here**: whether a built worktree's installed package answers the probe above. The shared checkout `/home/user/objectui` has **no `node_modules`**, so a probe taken there returns a **dead-instrument zero**, ⛔ not a reading.
